Este es el hombre que por todas partes enseña a todos contra nuestro pueblo, contra la ley y contra este lugar. ¡Y ahora hasta ha metido griegos en el templo y ha profanado este lugar santo!».
es.R: Los siete días casi habían terminado. Entonces unos judíos de la provincia de Asia vieron a Pablo en el templo. Alborotaron a toda la gente y agarraron a Pablo. \v 28 Gritaban: «Pueblo de Israel, ¡{{plural_you:ayúdennos|ayudadnos}}! Este hombre va por todas partes enseñando a todos cosas contra nuestro pueblo, contra la ley de Dios y contra este templo. ¡Y ahora ha metido griegos en el templo, y ha hecho impuro este lugar santo!».

decisions.choice: the seven days: the days of purification of 21:24-26
alternatives: the seven days of the feast of Pentecost
decisions.reason: Cleansing took seven days (Numbers 19:12). Paul had been purified and was keeping those days in the temple.

decisions.choice: the Jews from Asia: Jews from the province of Asia, in Jerusalem for the feast
decisions.reason: Asia was the Roman province whose chief city was Ephesus, where Jews had opposed Paul (19:9; 20:19). Paul hurried to Jerusalem for Pentecost (20:16). They knew Trophimus by sight (21:29).

decisions.choice: men, Israelites: a call to the people of Israel
alternatives: a call to the men only
decisions.reason: It is the formal way of addressing the people, as at 2:22 and 3:12. The cry goes to the whole crowd, though in the inner courts it may have been mostly men.

decisions.choice: bringing Greeks into the temple: taking Gentiles past the barrier into the inner courts
alternatives: bringing them into the outer court, which was open to all
decisions.reason: Gentiles could enter the outer court, but a low wall barred them from the courts beyond. Josephus describes notices on it in Greek and Latin forbidding foreigners to enter (Jewish War 5.193-194), and one of these warning inscriptions, threatening death, has been found.

decisions.choice: against the people, the law and this place: the charge once made against Stephen
decisions.reason: False witnesses said Stephen spoke against this holy place and the law (6:13-14).

decisions.choice: has defiled: made common, made unclean
decisions.reason: The verb means to make common, the opposite of holy (10:14-15).

decisions.choice: People of Israel, with "Men of Israel" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The inclusive default follows the meaning note; Literal keeps "men".

decisions.choice: God's law; this temple
decisions.reason: Readable says which law and which place.

decisions.choice: {{gender:Israélites|Hommes d’Israël}} (B)
decisions.reason: French "Israélites" already takes in men and women, and as an address it is shorter and closer to the Greek than "Peuple d’Israël", which Readable uses; "Hommes d’Israël" stays as the traditional alternative. Literal keeps "Hommes israélites", as English Literal keeps "Men".

decisions.choice: Hombres israelitas (L); {{gender:Israelitas|Hombres de Israel}} (B); Pueblo de Israel (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:22: Literal keeps the formal address; Balanced has the gender setting as the English does; Readable speaks to the whole people, as the English Readable does (meaning decision on "men, Israelites").

source.text: ἦσαν γὰρ προεωρακότες Τρόφιμον τὸν Ἐφέσιον ἐν τῇ πόλει σὺν αὐτῷ, ὃν ἐνόμιζον ὅτι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν εἰσήγαγεν ὁ Παῦλος.

records.literal_gloss: They were for having previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, whom they were supposing that into the temple brought Paul.

en.L: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.
en.B: For they had seen Paul in the city a little earlier with Trophimus, a man of Ephesus, and they took it for granted that Paul had taken him into the temple.
en.R: They said this because they had seen Paul in the city with Trophimus, a Gentile from Ephesus. They thought Paul had taken him into the temple.

fr.L: Car ils avaient vu auparavant Trophime l’Éphésien dans la ville avec lui, et ils supposaient que Paul l’avait fait entrer dans le temple.
fr.B: Ils avaient en effet vu un peu plus tôt Paul en ville avec Trophime, un homme d’Éphèse, et ils tenaient pour acquis que Paul l’avait fait entrer dans le temple.
fr.R: Ils disaient cela parce qu’ils avaient vu Paul dans la ville avec Trophime, un non-Juif d’Éphèse. Ils pensaient que Paul l’avait fait entrer dans le temple.

es.L: Porque antes habían visto con él en la ciudad a Trófimo el efesio, a quien suponían que Pablo había metido en el templo.
es.B: Es que poco antes habían visto a Pablo en la ciudad con Trófimo, un hombre de Éfeso, y dieron por hecho que Pablo lo había llevado al templo.
es.R: Decían esto porque habían visto a Pablo en la ciudad con Trófimo, un gentil de Éfeso. Pensaron que Pablo lo había llevado al templo.

decisions.choice: Trophimus the Ephesian: a Gentile believer from Asia who traveled with Paul
decisions.reason: Trophimus was one of those who went with Paul (20:4). Paul later left him sick at Miletus (2 Timothy 4:20). As a Gentile he could not go beyond the outer court.

decisions.choice: they supposed: they assumed it, wrongly
decisions.reason: Luke uses this verb for a belief that turns out false (14:19, 16:27). He reports that they had seen Trophimus with Paul in the city, not in the temple.

decisions.choice: They said this because
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the link to the cry in 21:28.

decisions.choice: a Gentile from Ephesus
decisions.reason: Readable says why it mattered, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ἐκινήθη τε ἡ πόλις ὅλη καὶ ἐγένετο συνδρομὴ τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενοι τοῦ Παύλου εἷλκον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ εὐθέως ἐκλείσθησαν αἱ θύραι.

records.literal_gloss: Was moved then the city whole and there was a running together of the people, and having seized Paul they were dragging him outside the temple, and immediately were shut the doors.

en.L: And the whole city was stirred, and there was a running together of the people, and having seized Paul, they dragged him outside the temple, and immediately the doors were shut.
en.B: The entire city was set in motion, and the people rushed together. They laid hold of Paul and hauled him out of the temple, and straightaway the gates were closed.
en.R: The whole city became upset, and people came running together. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Right away the temple gates were shut.

fr.L: Et toute la ville fut en émoi, et il y eut un attroupement du peuple ; et s’étant saisis de Paul, ils le traînaient hors du temple, et aussitôt les portes furent fermées.
fr.B: Toute la ville s’agita, et le peuple accourut en masse. Ils s’emparèrent de Paul et le traînèrent hors du temple, et aussitôt on ferma les portes.
fr.R: Toute la ville s’est agitée, et les gens sont arrivés en courant. Ils ont saisi Paul et ils l’ont traîné hors du temple. Tout de suite, on a fermé les portes du temple.

es.L: Y toda la ciudad se agitó, y hubo un tumulto del pueblo, y agarrando a Pablo, lo arrastraban fuera del templo, y al instante se cerraron las puertas.
es.B: Toda la ciudad se puso en movimiento, y la gente acudió corriendo. Agarraron a Pablo y lo sacaron a rastras del templo, y enseguida se cerraron las puertas.
es.R: Toda la ciudad se alborotó, y la gente llegó corriendo. Agarraron a Pablo y lo arrastraron fuera del templo. Enseguida se cerraron las puertas del templo.

decisions.choice: the doors: the gates between the inner courts and the outer court
alternatives: the outer gates of the whole temple area
decisions.reason: Paul was dragged out of the inner courts into the outer court, and the temple guards (4:1) shut the gates behind him. The text does not say why; perhaps to keep the holy place from further defilement or from bloodshed.

decisions.choice: a running together: people rushing in from all sides
decisions.reason: The noun is used of a crowd running together.

decisions.choice: they were dragging him: the action is shown as it went on
decisions.reason: The imperfect pictures the scene as it happened.

decisions.choice: gates
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of doors they were, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ζητούντων τε αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἀνέβη φάσις τῷ χιλιάρχῳ τῆς σπείρης ὅτι ὅλη συγχύννεται Ἰερουσαλήμ, ὃς ἐξαυτῆς παραλαβὼν στρατιώτας καὶ ἑκατοντάρχας κατέδραμεν ἐπ’ αὐτούς, οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες τὸν χιλίαρχον καὶ τοὺς στρατιώτας ἐπαύσαντο τύπτοντες τὸν Παῦλον.

records.literal_gloss: Seeking then [they] him to kill, went up a report to the tribune of the cohort that all is in confusion Jerusalem; \v 32 who at once having taken soldiers and centurions ran down upon them; they then having seen the tribune and the soldiers stopped beating Paul.

en.L: And while they were seeking to kill him, a report went up to the tribune of the cohort that all Jerusalem was in confusion. \v 32 He at once took soldiers and centurions and ran down upon them, and when they saw the tribune and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
en.B: They were set on killing him when a report went up to the tribune in command of the cohort that the whole of Jerusalem was in turmoil. \v 32 He immediately took soldiers and centurions and rushed down on the crowd, and at the sight of the tribune and the soldiers they left off beating Paul.
en.R: They were trying to kill Paul. Then someone told the tribune, the commander of the Roman soldiers in Jerusalem, that the whole city was in an uproar. \v 32 Right away the tribune took soldiers and their officers, called centurions, and ran down to the crowd. When the people saw the tribune and the soldiers, they stopped hitting Paul.

fr.L: Et comme ils cherchaient à le tuer, la nouvelle monta jusqu’au tribun de la cohorte que tout Jérusalem était en confusion. \v 32 Celui-ci, aussitôt, prit des soldats et des centurions et descendit vers eux en courant ; et eux, voyant le tribun et les soldats, cessèrent de frapper Paul.
fr.B: Ils cherchaient à le tuer quand la nouvelle monta jusqu’au tribun qui commandait la cohorte : tout Jérusalem était en ébullition. \v 32 Il prit aussitôt des soldats et des centurions et se précipita sur la foule ; à la vue du tribun et des soldats, ils cessèrent de frapper Paul.
fr.R: Ils essayaient de tuer Paul. Alors quelqu’un a dit au tribun, le commandant des soldats romains à Jérusalem, que toute la ville était en pleine agitation. \v 32 Aussitôt, le tribun a pris des soldats et leurs officiers, qu’on appelle des centurions, et il a couru vers la foule. Quand les gens ont vu le tribun et les soldats, ils ont arrêté de frapper Paul.

es.L: Y mientras procuraban matarlo, subió aviso al tribuno de la cohorte de que toda Jerusalén estaba alborotada; \v 32 el cual, tomando al instante soldados y centuriones, bajó corriendo hacia ellos; y ellos, al ver al tribuno y a los soldados, dejaron de golpear a Pablo.
es.B: Estaban a punto de matarlo cuando llegó al tribuno que mandaba la cohorte la noticia de que toda Jerusalén estaba alborotada. \v 32 Enseguida tomó soldados y centuriones y bajó corriendo hacia la multitud. Al ver al tribuno y a los soldados, dejaron de golpear a Pablo.
es.R: Querían matar a Pablo. Entonces alguien le avisó al tribuno, el comandante de los soldados romanos en Jerusalén, que toda la ciudad estaba alborotada. \v 32 Enseguida el tribuno tomó soldados y a sus oficiales, llamados centuriones, y bajó corriendo hasta la multitud. Cuando la gente vio al tribuno y a los soldados, dejaron de golpear a Pablo.

decisions.choice: the tribune of the cohort: the Roman officer commanding the troops in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: A tribune was a Roman officer; the title means commander of a thousand. A cohort was a unit of several hundred soldiers. This cohort was kept in the Antonia fortress beside the temple. The tribune's name was Claudius Lysias (23:26).

decisions.choice: went up; ran down: the fortress stood above the temple courts
decisions.reason: Josephus says the Antonia fortress overlooked the temple from the northwest, with stairs down to the colonnades, and that soldiers watched the crowds there at the feasts (Jewish War 5.238-247).

decisions.choice: centurions: officers over about a hundred soldiers each
decisions.reason: The plural shows the tribune took a large force, perhaps two hundred men or more.

decisions.choice: they stopped beating Paul: the crowd had been beating him
alternatives: they did not start to beat him
decisions.reason: The verb means to stop doing something already under way.

decisions.choice: the commander of the Roman soldiers in Jerusalem; their officers, called centurions
alternatives: the tribune of the cohort; centurions
decisions.reason: Readable says who the tribune and the centurions were, as the meaning notes explain.

decisions.choice: the tribune in command of the cohort
decisions.reason: Balanced says how the tribune was related to the cohort.

decisions.choice: le tribun, la cohorte; des centurions at every level, Readable saying who they were
decisions.reason: "Tribun" and "cohorte" are the French words for these Roman ranks and units, and English keeps "tribune" at every level; Readable explains both words as English Readable does. The term sheet keeps "centurion" at Literal and Balanced and lets Readable follow the English, which here keeps the word with an explanation.

decisions.choice: el tribuno (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The Spanish title of the Roman officer, as in 24:22 and 25:23 (meaning decision on the tribune of the cohort); Readable adds who he was, as the English Readable does. "Centuriones" likewise, with "sus oficiales" at Readable.

source.text: τότε ἐγγίσας ὁ χιλίαρχος ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκέλευσε δεθῆναι ἁλύσεσι δυσί, καὶ ἐπυνθάνετο τίς εἴη καὶ τί ἐστιν πεποιηκώς.

records.literal_gloss: Then having drawn near the tribune seized him and ordered [him] to be bound with chains two, and was inquiring who he might be and what he has been doing.

en.L: Then the tribune came near, seized him, and ordered [him] to be bound with two chains, and he inquired who he might be and what he had done.
en.B: Coming up to Paul, the tribune took him into custody and gave orders to fasten him with two chains. He began asking who the man was and what he had been doing.
en.R: The tribune came over and arrested Paul. He told his soldiers to put two chains on him. Then he asked the people who this man was and what he had done.

fr.L: Alors le tribun, s’étant approché, se saisit de lui et ordonna qu’on le lie de deux chaînes ; et il demandait qui il pouvait être et ce qu’il avait fait.
fr.B: Le tribun s’approcha, fit arrêter Paul et ordonna qu’on l’attache avec deux chaînes. Puis il se mit à demander qui était cet homme et ce qu’il avait fait.
fr.R: Le tribun s’est approché et il a arrêté Paul. Il a dit à ses soldats de lui mettre deux chaînes. Puis il a demandé aux gens qui était cet homme et ce qu’il avait fait.

es.L: Entonces, acercándose el tribuno, lo prendió y mandó que lo ataran con dos cadenas, y preguntaba quién era y qué había hecho.
es.B: El tribuno se acercó, lo arrestó y dio orden de que lo sujetaran con dos cadenas. Luego preguntó quién era aquel hombre y qué había hecho.
es.R: El tribuno se acercó y arrestó a Pablo. Mandó a sus soldados que le pusieran dos cadenas. Luego le preguntó a la gente quién era ese hombre y qué había hecho.

decisions.choice: two chains: Paul was most likely chained to a soldier on each side
decisions.reason: Peter was held the same way, between two soldiers with two chains (12:6).

decisions.choice: bound: Agabus's word begins to come true
decisions.reason: Agabus said Paul would be bound in Jerusalem and handed over to the Gentiles (21:11). Now a Roman officer binds him.

decisions.choice: he inquired: he asked the crowd, not Paul
decisions.reason: The answers come from the crowd (21:34). The question "who he might be" shows he did not know whom he had arrested.

decisions.choice: asked the people
decisions.reason: Readable names whom he asked, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ἄλλοι δὲ ἄλλο τι ἐπεφώνουν ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ· μὴ δυναμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς διὰ τὸν θόρυβον ἐκέλευσεν ἄγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν.

records.literal_gloss: Others however something other were shouting in the crowd; not being able then he to know the certain [thing] because of the uproar, he ordered him to be brought into the barracks.

en.L: But some in the crowd were shouting one thing, others another, and since he could not learn the facts because of the uproar, he ordered him to be brought into the barracks.
en.B: But the crowd shouted back, some one thing, some another. The din made it impossible for him to get at the facts, so he had Paul taken into the barracks.
en.R: Some people in the crowd shouted one thing, and others shouted something else. There was so much noise that the tribune could not find out what had really happened. So he ordered his soldiers to take Paul into the fortress where they lived.

fr.L: Mais dans la foule, les uns criaient une chose, les autres une autre ; et comme il ne pouvait rien apprendre de certain à cause du tumulte, il ordonna qu’on le conduise dans la caserne.
fr.B: Mais dans la foule, les uns criaient ceci, les autres cela. Le vacarme l’empêchant de savoir ce qui s’était réellement passé, il fit conduire Paul dans la caserne.
fr.R: Dans la foule, certains criaient une chose, et d’autres criaient autre chose. Il y avait tant de bruit que le tribun ne pouvait pas savoir ce qui s’était vraiment passé. Alors il a donné l’ordre à ses soldats d’emmener Paul dans la forteresse où ils logeaient.

es.L: Pero entre la multitud unos gritaban una cosa y otros otra; y como no podía saber con certeza [lo ocurrido] a causa del alboroto, mandó que lo llevaran al cuartel.
es.B: Pero entre la multitud unos gritaban una cosa y otros otra. Con tanto alboroto no podía averiguar los hechos, así que mandó llevar a Pablo al cuartel.
es.R: Algunas personas de la multitud gritaban una cosa, y otras gritaban otra. Había tanto ruido que el tribuno no pudo saber qué había pasado de verdad. Por eso mandó a sus soldados que llevaran a Pablo a la fortaleza donde vivían.

decisions.choice: the barracks: the soldiers' quarters in the Antonia fortress
decisions.reason: The word means a camp or barracks. Here it is the quarters of the cohort in the fortress beside the temple (21:31).

decisions.choice: the facts: what was certain
decisions.reason: The word means what is firm or certain, as in 22:30 and 25:26.

decisions.choice: some shouted one thing, some another: a crowd in confusion
decisions.reason: Luke describes the town assembly at Ephesus the same way (19:32).

decisions.choice: the fortress where they lived
decisions.reason: Readable says what the barracks were, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀναβαθμούς, συνέβη βαστάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν στρατιωτῶν διὰ τὴν βίαν τοῦ ὄχλου, ἠκολούθει γὰρ τὸ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ κράζοντες· Αἶρε αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: When now he came upon the stairs, it happened [that] to be carried he by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd; \v 36 were following for the multitude of the people, crying out, Away with him!

en.L: And when he came to the stairs, it happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd, \v 36 for the multitude of the people kept following, crying out, "Away with him!"
en.B: At the stairs, the crowd's violence was such that the soldiers had to carry Paul up. \v 36 The whole mass of people came after them, crying out, "Away with him!"
en.R: When they came to the steps of the fortress, the crowd was so wild that the soldiers had to carry Paul. \v 36 The whole crowd followed them and kept shouting, "Kill him!"

fr.L: Et quand il fut sur les marches, il arriva qu’il fut porté par les soldats à cause de la violence de la foule, \v 36 car la multitude du peuple suivait en criant : « Fais-le disparaître ! »
fr.B: Arrivé aux marches, Paul dut être porté par les soldats, tant la foule était violente. \v 36 Toute la masse du peuple les suivait en criant : « Fais-le disparaître ! »
fr.R: Quand ils sont arrivés aux marches de la forteresse, la foule était si violente que les soldats ont dû porter Paul. \v 36 Toute la foule les suivait et criait sans arrêt : « Tuez-le ! »

es.L: Y cuando llegó a las gradas, sucedió que fue llevado en peso por los soldados a causa de la violencia de la multitud, \v 36 porque la muchedumbre del pueblo seguía detrás, gritando: «¡Fuera con él!».
es.B: Al llegar a las escaleras, la violencia de la multitud era tal que los soldados tuvieron que llevar a Pablo en peso. \v 36 Toda la muchedumbre iba detrás de ellos gritando: «¡Fuera con él!».
es.R: Cuando llegaron a las escaleras de la fortaleza, la multitud estaba tan furiosa que los soldados tuvieron que cargar a Pablo. \v 36 Toda la multitud los seguía y gritaba: «¡Que lo maten!».

decisions.choice: the stairs: the steps from the temple's outer court up to the fortress
alternatives: the steps of the inner courts
decisions.reason: Josephus says stairs led down from the Antonia to the colonnades of the temple (Jewish War 5.243).

decisions.choice: Away with him: the cry raised against Jesus
decisions.reason: The crowd cried the same words before Pilate (Luke 23:18; John 19:15). In 22:22 they add that such a man should not be allowed to live, so it is a call for his death.

decisions.choice: for: the crowd pressing after them explains why Paul was carried
decisions.reason: The word "for" ties the following crowd to the violence in 21:35.

decisions.choice: Kill him!
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cry meant, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: Fais-le disparaître ! (L, B); Tuez-le ! (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek cry is a singular command, as if to the tribune, and asks for the man to be done away with; "Fais-le disparaître" keeps both. "À mort" would say only what the cry meant, which Readable says, as English Readable does.

source.text: Μέλλων τε εἰσάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν ὁ Παῦλος λέγει τῷ χιλιάρχῳ· Εἰ ἔξεστίν μοι εἰπεῖν τι πρὸς σέ;

records.literal_gloss: Being about then to be brought into the barracks Paul says to the tribune, If it is permitted to me to say something to you?

en.L: And as he was about to be brought into the barracks, Paul says to the tribune, "Is it permitted for me to say something to you?"
en.B: As they were about to take him into the barracks, Paul said to the tribune, "May I have a word with you?"
en.R: The soldiers were about to take Paul into the fortress. Then Paul said to the tribune, "Please, may I speak with you?"

fr.L: Et comme il allait être conduit dans la caserne, Paul dit au tribun : « M’est-il permis de te dire quelque chose ? »
fr.B: Au moment où on allait le faire entrer dans la caserne, Paul dit au tribun : « Puis-je te dire un mot ? »
fr.R: Les soldats allaient faire entrer Paul dans la forteresse. Alors Paul a dit au tribun : « S’il te plaît, est-ce que je peux te parler ? »

es.L: Y estando para ser introducido en el cuartel, Pablo dice al tribuno: «¿Me es permitido decirte algo?».
es.B: Cuando estaban a punto de meterlo en el cuartel, Pablo le dijo al tribuno: «¿Puedo decirte una palabra?».
es.R: Los soldados estaban a punto de meter a Pablo en la fortaleza. Entonces Pablo le dijo al tribuno: «Por favor, ¿puedo hablar contigo?».

decisions.choice: a direct question, opened with the word for "if"
alternatives: "if I may say something", an unfinished sentence
decisions.reason: Greek of the time could open a direct question this way (1:6, 19:2).

decisions.choice: says: a present tense in a past story
decisions.reason: Luke uses the present to make the scene vivid; the event itself is past.

decisions.choice: Paul asks in Greek, the common language of the eastern empire
decisions.reason: The tribune's surprise in 21:37-38 shows that Paul spoke to him in Greek.

decisions.choice: said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: tu between Paul and the tribune
decisions.reason: The style guide uses "tu" for one person, following the Greek singular, so Paul and the Roman officer say "tu" to each other. Paul's courtesy shows in his words ("Puis-je", "S’il te plaît"), not in "vous".

decisions.choice: decirte (tú)
decisions.reason: As across the Spanish New Testament, a single person is addressed with "tú", here Paul and the tribune speaking to each other; the courtesy of the request is carried by the question itself.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ἑλληνιστὶ γινώσκεις;

records.literal_gloss: He then was saying, Greek do you know?

en.L: And he said, "Do you know Greek?
en.B: The tribune said, "You know Greek?
en.R: The tribune said, "You can speak Greek?

fr.L: Et celui-ci dit : « Tu connais le grec ?
fr.B: Le tribun répondit : « Tu sais le grec ?
fr.R: Le tribun a dit : « Tu parles grec ?

es.L: Y él dijo: «¿Sabes griego?
es.B: El tribuno le dijo: «¿Sabes griego?
es.R: El tribuno le dijo: «¿Hablas griego?

decisions.choice: Greek: the Greek language
decisions.reason: The adverb means "in Greek"; with "know" it means knowing the language.

decisions.choice: the tribune's surprise
decisions.reason: He had taken Paul for a rebel from Egypt (21:38) and did not expect him to speak educated Greek.

decisions.choice: The tribune
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

source.text: οὐκ ἄρα σὺ εἶ ὁ Αἰγύπτιος ὁ πρὸ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀναστατώσας καὶ ἐξαγαγὼν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους ἄνδρας τῶν σικαρίων;

records.literal_gloss: Not then you are the Egyptian, the [one] before these the days having stirred up a revolt and having led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Sicarii?

en.L: Then are you not the Egyptian who before these days stirred up a revolt and led out into the wilderness the 4,000 men of the Sicarii?"
en.B: So you are not the Egyptian who stirred up a rebellion a while ago and led the 4,000 men of the Assassins out into the wilderness?"
en.R: I thought you were the Egyptian who started a rebellion some time ago. He led 4,000 armed men called Assassins out into the desert."

fr.L: Tu n’es donc pas l’Égyptien qui, avant ces jours-ci, a soulevé une révolte et a emmené au désert les quatre mille hommes des sicaires ? »
fr.B: Tu n’es donc pas l’Égyptien qui a soulevé une révolte il y a quelque temps et qui a entraîné au désert les quatre mille sicaires ? »
fr.R: Je croyais que tu étais l’Égyptien qui a commencé une révolte il y a quelque temps. Il a emmené dans le désert quatre mille tueurs armés de poignards. »

es.L: ¿No eres tú, pues, el egipcio que antes de estos días levantó una revuelta y sacó al desierto a los 4000 hombres de los sicarios?».
es.B: Entonces, ¿no eres tú el egipcio que hace un tiempo provocó una rebelión y llevó al desierto a los 4000 sicarios?».
es.R: Yo pensaba que eras el egipcio que comenzó una rebelión hace algún tiempo. Él llevó al desierto a 4000 hombres armados, llamados sicarios».

decisions.choice: So you are not the Egyptian: the tribune realizes he was mistaken
alternatives: "Are you not the Egyptian?", expecting the answer yes
decisions.reason: The two opening words usually mark surprise at something just learned: a man who speaks Greek like this is not who he thought. Others read the question as expecting Paul to say he is the Egyptian.

decisions.choice: the Egyptian: a rebel known from Josephus
decisions.reason: Josephus tells of an Egyptian false prophet in the time of Felix who gathered followers in the wilderness and led them to the Mount of Olives, saying Jerusalem's walls would fall at his command. Felix's troops scattered them and the Egyptian escaped (Jewish War 2.261-263; Antiquities 20.169-172). Josephus gives larger numbers, and his two accounts differ.

decisions.choice: the Sicarii: the "dagger men", a group of assassins
decisions.reason: The word is borrowed from Latin and means men with daggers. Josephus says that under Felix they killed opponents in the festival crowds in Jerusalem with short daggers hidden in their clothes (Jewish War 2.254-257). Luke links the Egyptian's followers with them; Josephus describes the two separately.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: the desert country
decisions.reason: The word means empty, uninhabited land, like the wilderness of Judea.

decisions.choice: the Sicarii
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the borrowed Latin word, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: Assassins
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable translate the name; "Assassins" says what they did without a modern label.

decisions.choice: a statement: I thought you were the Egyptian
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question implies, as the first meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: les sicaires (L, B); des tueurs armés de poignards (R)
decisions.reason: French has the word "sicaire" (a hired killer, from the same Latin word), so Balanced can keep it where English Balanced translates the name; "les Assassins" would recall the medieval sect. Readable says what they were, the "dagger men" of the meaning note.

decisions.choice: los sicarios
decisions.reason: Spanish "sicario" comes from this very name, the "dagger men" (meaning decision on the Sicarii), and still means a hired killer, so it serves at every level where the English Balanced and Readable say "Assassins".

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος· Ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος μέν εἰμι Ἰουδαῖος, Ταρσεὺς τῆς Κιλικίας, οὐκ ἀσήμου πόλεως πολίτης· δέομαι δέ σου, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι λαλῆσαι πρὸς τὸν λαόν.

records.literal_gloss: Said however Paul, I a man indeed am a Jew, of Tarsus of Cilicia, not of an insignificant city a citizen; I beg now you, allow me to speak to the people.

en.L: But Paul said, "I am a Jewish man, of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. And I beg you, allow me to speak to the people."
en.B: Paul answered, "I am a Jew, a man of Tarsus in Cilicia, and a citizen of a city of some note. I ask you, allow me to address the people."
en.R: Paul answered, "No, I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia. Tarsus is an important city, and I am a citizen there. Please let me speak to the people."

fr.L: Mais Paul dit : « Moi, je suis un homme juif, de Tarse en Cilicie, citoyen d’une ville qui n’est pas sans renom. Et je t’en prie, permets-moi de parler au peuple. »
fr.B: Paul répondit : « Je suis juif, originaire de Tarse en Cilicie, citoyen d’une ville de quelque importance. Je te prie, permets-moi de parler au peuple. »
fr.R: Paul a répondu : « Non, je suis juif, je viens de Tarse, en Cilicie. Tarse est une ville importante, et j’en suis citoyen. S’il te plaît, laisse-moi parler au peuple. »

es.L: Pero Pablo dijo: «Yo soy un hombre judío, de Tarso de Cilicia, ciudadano de una ciudad no insignificante. Y te ruego que me permitas hablar al pueblo».
es.B: Pablo le respondió: «Yo soy judío, de Tarso de Cilicia, ciudadano de una ciudad importante. Te pido que me permitas hablarle al pueblo».
es.R: Pablo respondió: «No, soy judío, de Tarso, en Cilicia. Tarso es una ciudad importante, y yo soy ciudadano de allí. Por favor, déjame hablarle a la gente».

decisions.choice: I am a Jew ... now I ask: the first part answers the question, the second makes a request
decisions.reason: The paired particles set Paul's answer, that he is a Jew and not the Egyptian, beside his request.

decisions.choice: Tarsus: the chief city of Cilicia, known for its schools
decisions.reason: Tarsus lay in the southeast of what is now Turkey. "No insignificant city" is understatement for a city of some fame. Paul was born there (9:11, 22:3).

decisions.choice: citizen: a citizen of Tarsus
decisions.reason: Paul speaks here of his city. That he is also a Roman citizen comes out in 22:25-28.

decisions.choice: the people: the Jewish crowd
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for the people of Israel (21:28, 21:30, 21:36).

decisions.choice: a city of some note
decisions.reason: Balanced states the understatement plainly, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: No
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Paul's answer denies being the Egyptian, as the first meaning note explains.

source.text: ἐπιτρέψαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος ἑστὼς ἐπὶ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν κατέσεισε τῇ χειρὶ τῷ λαῷ, πολλῆς δὲ σιγῆς γενομένης προσεφώνησεν τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ λέγων

records.literal_gloss: Having allowed [him] then he, Paul having stood on the stairs motioned with the hand to the people; great then silence having come, he addressed [them] in the Hebrew language, saying,

en.L: And when he had given permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, motioned with [his] hand to the people, and when a great silence had come, he addressed [them] in the Hebrew dialect, saying:
en.B: The tribune gave permission, and Paul, standing on the steps, raised his hand to the people. When all had fallen silent, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language. He said:
en.R: The tribune said he could. So Paul stood on the steps and raised his hand to get the people's attention. They all became very quiet. Then Paul spoke to them in the Jews' own language. He said:

fr.L: Et lui l’ayant permis, Paul, debout sur les marches, fit signe de la main au peuple ; et un grand silence s’étant fait, il prit la parole en dialecte hébreu, en disant :
fr.B: Le tribun le lui permit, et Paul, debout sur les marches, fit signe de la main au peuple. Quand tous se furent tus, il leur parla en langue hébraïque. Il dit :
fr.R: Le tribun a dit oui. Alors Paul s’est mis debout sur les marches, et il a levé la main pour que les gens l’écoutent. Tout le monde s’est tu. Puis Paul leur a parlé dans la langue des Juifs. Il a dit :

es.L: Y habiéndo[selo] permitido él, Pablo, de pie en las gradas, hizo señal con la mano al pueblo; y hecho un gran silencio, [les] habló en la lengua hebrea, diciendo:
es.B: El tribuno se lo permitió, y Pablo, de pie en las escaleras, hizo una señal con la mano al pueblo. Cuando todos guardaron silencio, les habló en la lengua hebrea. Les dijo:
es.R: El tribuno le dio permiso. Entonces Pablo se puso de pie en las escaleras y levantó la mano para que la gente le prestara atención. Todos se quedaron muy callados. Luego Pablo les habló en la lengua propia de los judíos. Les dijo:

decisions.choice: saying: the sentence runs on into Paul's speech, which begins at 22:1
decisions.reason: The chapter break falls between "saying" and the words Paul spoke, so this record ends with the speech still to come.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew language: the language of the Jews of the land, most likely Aramaic
alternatives: Hebrew, the language of the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Greek writers of the time used "Hebrew" both for Hebrew and for Aramaic, the everyday language of the Jews in Judea. John calls Aramaic place names "Hebrew" (John 19:13, 19:17). Paul could have used either, and the text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: motioning with the hand: a gesture asking for silence
decisions.reason: Peter and Paul make the same gesture before speaking (12:17, 13:16).

decisions.choice: speaking the people's own language won a hearing
decisions.reason: When they hear him speak in it, they grow even quieter (22:2).

decisions.choice: The tribune
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who gave permission.

decisions.choice: the Jews' own language
decisions.reason: Readable names the language by whose it was, which keeps open whether it was Hebrew or Aramaic, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: dialect; language
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek word; Balanced says language, which is what it means here.
